Developing Web Applications with KoldFusion

Developing Web Applications with KoldFusion

Welcome! This book is a quick, practical tour of the KoldFusion Markup Language (CFML). In an evening or two you will go from a one-line "hello" page to a small database application with forms, sessions, error handling and reusable components. Every chapter is short, and every example is live: click Run this example and the page runs on your own KoldFusion server, right next to the code that produced it.

Who this book is for

You should be comfortable writing HTML by hand (or at least unafraid of the "View Source" menu in Netscape Navigator) and know a little SQL: what a SELECT statement does and what a WHERE clause is for. You do not need to know C, Perl or Java. If you have ever built a static site and wished it could talk to a database, you are exactly who we had in mind.

For the full details of every tag and function, keep the CFML Language Reference open in another window. Server setup, data sources and security are covered in the Administrator's book.

How the book is organized

Chapter 1 introduces templates and the CFOUTPUT tag. Chapter 2 covers variables, expressions and the complex data types. Chapters 3 to 5 are about databases: reading data, collecting it with forms and writing it back. Chapter 6 ties pages together into an application with sessions. Chapter 7 deals with errors, and chapter 8 shows how to package code for reuse and how to send e-mail.

Conventions

Convention Meaning
CFQUERY Tag and function names. Click one to open its Language Reference page.
UPPERCASE tags Examples use uppercase tag and attribute names, the house style of the day. CFML itself does not care.
ch3_list.cfm Example file names. All examples live in /CFDOCS/devguide/examples/.
Run this example Opens the example in a separate browser window named "kfrun".
View source Shows the example's source exactly as it is stored on the server.

Note  The examples are written to be harmless: they only read data, or they put back whatever they change before the page finishes. E-mail examples send only to addresses at localhost.

The cfsnippets data source

All examples use the cfsnippets data source, which is installed and registered with the server. It is a small database of a fictional company and the odds and ends of its web site:

Table Columns What is in it
Employees Emp_ID, FirstName, LastName, Email, Phone, Department, StartDate, Salary, Contract 25 staff members in six departments
Departments Dept_ID, Dept_Name, Location Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Accounting, Administration, Training
CourseList Course_ID, Dept_ID, CorNumber, CorName, CorLevel, CorDesc, LastUpdate A college course catalog (BIOL, CS, MATH, ...)
Parks ParkName, ParkType, Region, State, City 42 national parks, monuments and historic sites
Products ProductID, Name, Description, Price, Category, InStock A computer store: modems, Zip disks, software
GuestBook ID, Name, Email, Comments, Posted Entries from the company guest book
Comments CommentID, Email, FromUser, Subject, CommtType, MessText, Posted, Processed Visitor feedback
Messages MsgID, ParentID, Subject, Author, Body, Posted A small threaded discussion forum

You can browse the tables with the Administrator's data source tools, or simply run the examples in chapter 3.
